pharm: Selective, orally bioavailable inhibitor of cyclin-dependent kinases 4 and 6 that blocks phosphorylation of the retinoblastoma protein (Rb), arresting tumor cells in the G1 phase of the cell cycle and inhibiting proliferation of hormone-receptor-positive breast cancer cells; used in combination with endocrine therapy.
quick: 150 mg twice daily with endocrine therapy; 200 mg twice daily as monotherapy
Take with or without food, at about the same times each day
Can cause fetal harm; avoid - use effective contraception
Do not breastfeed during and for 3 weeks after the last dose
No adjustment in mild-moderate; not studied in severe/ESRD
Reduce to once-daily dosing frequency in severe impairment (Child-Pugh C)
No specific interaction; limit due to additive hepatic/GI effects
CBC, LFTs, diarrhea, signs of ILD/pneumonitis and VTE
summary: Abemaciclib is an oral inhibitor of cyclin-dependent kinases 4 and 6 (CDK4/6) used to treat hormone-receptor (HR)-positive, HER2-negative breast cancer. It is given in combination with endocrine therapy (an aromatase inhibitor, tamoxifen, or fulvestrant) for adjuvant treatment of high-risk node-positive early disease and for advanced/metastatic disease, and as monotherapy after progression on prior endocrine therapy and chemotherapy in the metastatic setting. By blocking CDK4/6, it prevents Rb phosphorylation and halts the cell cycle in G1. Diarrhea is very common and often occurs early; other important risks are neutropenia, hepatotoxicity, interstitial lung disease/pneumonitis, and venous thromboembolism. It is a CYP3A4 substrate, so dose adjustment is needed with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors and the combination with strong inducers should be avoided.
indications: In combination with endocrine therapy (tamoxifen or an aromatase inhibitor) for adjuvant treatment of adults with HR-positive, HER2-negative, node-positive early breast cancer at high risk of recurrence
In combination with an aromatase inhibitor as initial endocrine-based therapy for HR-positive, HER2-negative advanced or metastatic breast cancer in adults
In combination with fulvestrant for HR-positive, HER2-negative advanced or metastatic breast cancer with disease progression following endocrine therapy
As monotherapy for HR-positive, HER2-negative advanced or metastatic breast cancer with disease progression following endocrine therapy and prior chemotherapy in the metastatic setting

dosage.c: In combination with endocrine therapy (aromatase inhibitor, tamoxifen, or fulvestrant)
dosage.n: Continue until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity; for adjuvant use, continue endocrine therapy as clinically indicated

dosage.c: Monotherapy (metastatic, after endocrine therapy and chemotherapy)
dosage.n: Continue until progression or unacceptable toxicity

dosage.d: 100 mg twice daily (from 150 mg) or 150 mg twice daily (from 200 mg)
dosage.n: Reduce stepwise for diarrhea, hematologic, hepatic, or other toxicity per label tables

dosage.d: Reduce dosing frequency to once daily
dosage.n: Keep the same dose level but give once daily

dosage.c: With concomitant strong CYP3A4 inhibitor (when unavoidable)
dosage.d: Reduce dose to 100 mg twice daily (or 50 mg twice daily if already reduced)
dosage.n: Avoid strong CYP3A4 inhibitors where possible

admin: Take tablets orally with or without food at approximately the same times each day
Swallow tablets whole; do not chew, crush, or split them
If a dose is missed or the patient vomits, do not replace it - take the next dose at the scheduled time
At the first sign of loose stools, start an antidiarrheal (e.g., loperamide), increase oral fluids, and notify the prescriber
Obtain CBC and liver function tests before starting, then periodically, and interrupt/reduce/discontinue per toxicity tables
moa: Abemaciclib is a potent and selective inhibitor of cyclin-dependent kinases 4 and 6 (CDK4 and CDK6). In hormone-receptor-positive breast cancer, cyclin D1-CDK4/6 complexes phosphorylate the retinoblastoma tumor-suppressor protein (Rb), releasing E2F transcription factors and driving progression from G1 into S phase of the cell cycle. By inhibiting CDK4/6, abemaciclib prevents Rb phosphorylation, blocks cell-cycle progression, and induces G1 arrest, reducing tumor cell proliferation. Continuous twice-daily dosing achieves sustained target inhibition. Combination with endocrine therapy produces greater and more durable suppression of estrogen-driven proliferation than endocrine therapy alone.

absolute: Known serious hypersensitivity to abemaciclib or any excipient
relative: History of or active venous thromboembolism
Concomitant strong CYP3A4 inhibitors or inducers
monitor: Pulmonary symptoms (dyspnea, cough, hypoxia) for ILD/pneumonitis
Signs and symptoms of deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism

preg: Based on its mechanism and animal findings, abemaciclib can cause fetal harm. Verify pregnancy status before starting in females of reproductive potential and advise use of effective contraception during treatment and for at least 3 weeks after the last dose. Do not use during pregnancy unless the benefit clearly outweighs the risk.
lact: It is not known whether abemaciclib is present in human milk or its effects on the breastfed infant or milk production. Because of the potential for serious adverse reactions in a breastfed child, advise women not to breastfeed during treatment and for 3 weeks after the final dose.
renal: No dose adjustment is required for mild or moderate renal impairment. Abemaciclib has not been studied in patients with severe renal impairment, end-stage renal disease, or on dialysis; use with caution and monitor closely.
hepatic: No dose adjustment is needed for mild (Child-Pugh A) or moderate (Child-Pugh B) hepatic impairment. For severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh C), reduce the dosing frequency to once daily. Monitor liver function tests throughout treatment and modify or discontinue for hepatotoxicity.

major: Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g., ketoconazole, clarithromycin, ritonavir) - increase abemaciclib exposure; avoid or reduce abemaciclib dose
Strong CYP3A4 inducers (e.g., rifampin, carbamazepine, phenytoin, St John's wort) - decrease exposure and efficacy; avoid concomitant use
moderate: Moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors - may increase exposure; monitor for toxicity
minor: Abemaciclib does not significantly inhibit major CYP enzymes at clinical concentrations
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food; grapefruit and grapefruit juice (CYP3A4 inhibition) should be avoided.
interactions.alcohol: No specific interaction is described; limit alcohol because of additive potential for hepatic and gastrointestinal effects.
interactions.diagnostics: Increases serum creatinine by inhibiting renal tubular transporters (OCT2, MATE1/2-K) without reducing true GFR; interpret rises in creatinine in this context and assess actual renal function if needed.

emergency: Severe or persistent diarrhea with dehydration
Febrile neutropenia or signs of serious infection
New or worsening dyspnea, cough, or hypoxia (pneumonitis)
Symptoms of pulmonary embolism (sudden dyspnea, chest pain) or DVT

monitoring: Complete blood count before treatment, every 2 weeks for the first 2 months, monthly for the next 2 months, then as clinically indicated
Liver function tests before treatment and periodically
Diarrhea frequency/severity, hydration status, and electrolytes
Respiratory symptoms for interstitial lung disease/pneumonitis
Signs and symptoms of venous thromboembolism
Pregnancy status in females of reproductive potential before starting
counsel: Take your tablets twice a day at about the same times, with or without food, and swallow them whole
Diarrhea is common and can start in the first weeks - keep loperamide on hand, drink plenty of fluids, and start treatment at the first loose stool
Call your care team for diarrhea that does not improve, fever, or signs of infection
Report any new or worsening cough, shortness of breath, or chest discomfort right away
Tell your doctor about leg swelling, pain, or sudden breathlessness (possible blood clot)
Avoid grapefruit and tell your team about all other medicines; use effective birth control and do not breastfeed
pk: Cell-cycle arrest begins within days; clinical response over weeks
Plasma Tmax ~8 hours after oral dosing
Steady state in ~5 days with twice-daily dosing
pearls: Diarrhea is the most common and earliest toxicity - counsel on prompt loperamide use and hydration; dose-reduce/interrupt for grade >=2 that does not resolve
Causes a benign rise in serum creatinine by inhibiting tubular transporters - this does not reflect true loss of GFR
Has greater single-agent activity than other CDK4/6 inhibitors and is the only one approved as monotherapy
Interstitial lung disease/pneumonitis and venous thromboembolism are class-relevant serious risks - educate patients on warning signs
CYP3A4 substrate - avoid strong inducers; reduce dose with unavoidable strong inhibitors and avoid grapefruit
Verify pregnancy status, ensure contraception, and avoid breastfeeding during and for 3 weeks after therapy
missed: If you miss a dose or vomit after a dose, do not take an extra (replacement) dose. Take your next dose at the regularly scheduled time and continue your normal twice-daily schedule.
overdose: There is no known specific antidote. In overdose, provide general supportive care and monitor closely for fatigue and gastrointestinal effects (especially diarrhea), neutropenia, and hepatic toxicity, with management of fluid/electrolyte status and supportive measures as needed.
